transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm just really struggling with how my face looks, especially these horrible, deep scars and acne all over my cheeks. It feels like it's the first thing anyone notices when they look at me, and it completely ruins my appearance. I feel so self-conscious even just being here today.
Can you tell me more about these scars and acne on your cheeks, are they something that you spend a significant amount of time thinking about or trying to hide or fix every day?

Yes, I honestly can't stop thinking about them, and it's just so embarrassing and exhausting. I spend hours every morning trying to cover them up with layers of makeup, and I constantly pick at my skin to try and 'fix' the flaws, even though I know it probably makes them worse.
Aside from your concerns about your appearance, how have you been feeling overall, and have you noticed any changes in your interest in activities or hobbies that you usually enjoy?
I haven't really thought about my hobbies or noticed any changes there. I'm just so constantly preoccupied with how my face looks that I don't have the energy to focus on anything else right now.

How much of your daily life would you say is taken up by these thoughts and behaviors related to your appearance, and are there any situations or places where you avoid going because of how you feel about your face?

These thoughts and my routine of checking the mirror and trying to camouflage my face take up several hours every single day. Because of this, I completely avoid social gatherings, bright public spaces, and having my photo taken. I am just absolutely terrified of other people seeing my face under those lights.

Do you think your appearance would be significantly improved or would you feel significantly better about yourself if your scars and acne were to completely clear up, or are there other aspects of your appearance that also bother you?

Yes, I absolutely believe clearing up my scars and acne would make a massive difference in how I feel about myself. But honestly, I'm also deeply self-conscious and obsessed with other features, like the shape of my nose and how asymmetrical my face looks.

Are your concerns about your nose and the asymmetry of your face as distressing to you as your concerns about the scars and acne, or do you find that one aspect of your appearance bothers you more than the others at different times?

Both of them are deeply distressing and take up so much of my thoughts, but it definitely fluctuates. Some days I am completely obsessed with the asymmetry of my face and the shape of my nose, while other days the scars and acne feel completely unbearable and I can't focus on anything else.

Have you ever considered seeking professional help, such as a dermatologist or a plastic surgeon, to address your concerns about your appearance, and if so, what has held you back from pursuing these options?

I've actually already been to several dermatologists and plastic surgeons and have had multiple procedures done to try to fix my face. However, the results never seem to turn out right and I'm never satisfied, which is why I keep looking for new treatments to finally fix these flaws.

How do you think your life and overall well-being would change if you were able to find a treatment that you felt finally 'fixed' your appearance, and do you think that would alleviate all of your distress related to your body image?

I've always felt like fixing these flaws is the only way I could ever feel happy or normal. But honestly, I'm not entirely sure if it would solve every single problem in my life. It just feels like my appearance is the main thing holding me back from everything else.

Do you think that if your appearance were to change in the way you desire, you would still find yourself critically evaluating and being dissatisfied with other aspects of your appearance, or do you believe that resolving your current concerns would bring you lasting satisfaction?
I'm not really sure, and I haven't thought about it that way before. I just feel that if these specific flaws with my skin and face were finally fixed, I would finally feel okay.

Do you think that even if your current concerns about your appearance were fully addressed, you might still find new flaws or imperfections to focus on, or do you believe that resolving your current issues would lead to a more stable and lasting sense of self-acceptance?

I'm really not sure about that, and I haven't really thought about what would happen if these flaws were completely resolved. I'm just so focused on trying to fix my current problems that it's hard to imagine what my mindset would be like after.
